claims.text: What the image looks like IUP confirmed: intrauterine gestational sac with yolk sac (~5-6 wk); FHT by 6-7 wk; β-hCG discriminatory zone ~1500-2000 → intrauterine pregnancy
claims.quote: IUP confirmed: intrauterine gestational sac with yolk sac (~5-6 wk); FHT by 6-7 wk; β-hCG discriminatory zone ~1500-2000 Intrauterine pregnancy
claims.locator: Non-Trauma Ultrasound Findings, OB / Pelvic table

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) Diagnostic of an IUP: a gestational sac with a yolk sac or an embryo (with or without a heartbeat) within the uterine cavity
claims.quote: Ultrasonographic findings diagnostic of an intrauterine pregnancy are a gestational sac with a yolk sac or an embryo (with or without a heartbeat) within the uterine cavity.

claims.text: Gestational sac in the uterus: typically visible on ultrasound at about 4 to 5 weeks, typically at a serum beta-hCG of about 1500 mIU/mL; a yolk sac can usually be seen in it by 5 weeks
claims.quote: Presence of a gestational sac in the uterus, typically visible on ultrasound at about 4 to 5 weeks and typically corresponding to a serum beta-hCG level of about 1500 mIU/mL (a yolk sac can usually be seen in the gestational sac by 5 weeks)

claims.text: Fetal heart motion on ultrasound as early as 5 to 6 weeks; fetal heart sounds by handheld Doppler as early as 8 to 10 weeks if the uterus is accessible abdominally
claims.quote: Fetal heart motion visualized on ultrasound as early as 5 to 6 weeks Fetal heart sounds, heard with a handheld Doppler ultrasound device, as early as 8 to 10 weeks if the uterus is accessible abdominally

claims.text: Discriminatory zone: above it, ultrasound should be able to detect a gestational sac with a yolk sac, and a yolk sac confirms an IUP; for women with suspected ectopic pregnancy, to minimize overdiagnosis of ectopic pregnancy, the recommended threshold has been increased to 3500 mIU/mL
claims.quote: If serum beta-hCG is above a certain level (called the discriminatory zone), ultrasonography should be able to detect a gestational sac with a yolk sac; the presence of a yolk sac confirms an intrauterine pregnancy. The appropriate hCG threshold for the discriminatory zone for women with suspected ectopic pregnancy has been reevaluated. To minimize overdiagnosis of ectopic pregnancy and preserve desired intrauterine pregnancies, the recommended threshold has been increased to 3500 mIU/mL) (1).

claims.text: Usually urine (occasionally blood) tests are used to confirm or exclude pregnancy; results are typically accurate several days before a missed period
claims.quote: Usually urine and occasionally blood tests are used to confirm or exclude pregnancy; results are typically accurate several days before a missed menstrual period and often as early as several days after conception.

claims.text: Dating: when other information is lacking, first trimester ultrasound gives the most accurate gestational age; with an unknown conception date and irregular or unknown cycles, ultrasound may be the sole source of the EDD
claims.quote: When periods are regular, the menstrual history is a relatively reliable method of determining EDD. When other information is lacking, first trimester ultrasound provides the most accurate estimate of gestational age. When the date of conception is unknown and menstrual cycles are irregular or information about them is not available, ultrasound may be the sole source of the EDD.
claims.locator: Estimated Date of Delivery in Pregnancy

claims.text: The EDD is not changed based on ultrasounds after the first one; second and third trimester ultrasound should rarely be used to change gestational age
claims.quote: Reconciling the menstrual and ultrasonographic dates is done only after the first ultrasound in the current pregnancy—EDD is not changed based on subsequent ultrasounds. Because ultrasonographic estimates are less accurate later in pregnancy, second and third trimester ultrasonographic results should rarely be used to change estimated gestational age, and, if changing the estimated date of delivery is considered, a specialist in fetal ultrasonography should be consulted.
claims.locator: Estimated Date of Delivery in Pregnancy

claims.text: Causes Placental syncytial cells secrete beta-hCG beginning 10 days after fertilization; beta-hCG stimulates the corpus luteum to keep secreting estrogen and progesterone to maintain the pregnancy
claims.quote: Nausea and vomiting may occur because of increased secretion of estrogen and the beta subunit of human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG) by syncytial cells of the placenta, beginning 10 days after fertilization (see Conception and Prenatal Development). The corpus luteum in the ovary, stimulated by beta-hCG, continues secreting large amounts of estrogen and progesterone to maintain the pregnancy.

claims.text: Symptoms Nausea and vomiting may occur (estrogen and beta-hCG); many women become fatigued, and a few notice abdominal bloating very early
claims.quote: Nausea and vomiting may occur because of increased secretion of estrogen and the beta subunit of human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG) by syncytial cells of the placenta, beginning 10 days after fertilization (see Conception and Prenatal Development). The corpus luteum in the ovary, stimulated by beta-hCG, continues secreting large amounts of estrogen and progesterone to maintain the pregnancy. Many women become fatigued at this time, and a few women notice abdominal bloating very early.

claims.text: Women usually begin to feel fetal movement between 16 and 20 weeks
claims.quote: Women usually begin to feel fetal movement between 16 and 20 weeks.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Her chart: routine OB care

claims.text: Initial prenatal visit at 6 to 8 weeks; follow-up usually about every 4 weeks until 28 weeks, every 2 weeks from 28 to 36 weeks, then weekly to delivery; visits may be more frequent if there is a high risk of obstetric complications
claims.quote: The initial routine prenatal visit should occur between 6 and 8 weeks gestation. Follow-up visits usually occur at: About 4-week intervals until 28 weeks 2-week intervals from 28 to 36 weeks Weekly from 36 weeks to delivery Prenatal visits may be scheduled more frequently if there is a high risk of obstetric complications.

claims.text: EDD: LMP minus 3 months plus 7 days (Naegele's rule); or conception + 266 days; or LMP + 280 days (40 weeks) with regular 28-day cycles
claims.quote: The estimated date of delivery (EDD) is based on the last menstrual period (LMP). One way to calculate the EDD is to subtract 3 months from the LMP and add 7 days (Naegele's rule). Other methods are: The date of conception + 266 days The last menstrual period (LMP) + 280 days (40 weeks) for women with regular, 28-day menstrual cycles
